image_description: An underwater scene featuring a large hammerhead shark swimming diagonally from upper right to lower left. The shark has a distinct T-shaped head (cephalofoil) with eyes at the tips. The body is greyish-blue, blending with the water. Several smaller fish are visible in the background and foreground. The lighting is diffuse blue, typical of underwater photography.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The T-shaped head structure is clearly visible and defines the subject as a hammerhead.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots consistent with eyes are located at the very ends of the horizontal head extension.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution and water turbidity make it impossible to distinguish nostrils from the general texture of the cephalofoil underside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge appears relatively straight/slightly curved, consistent with the morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The torso tapers smoothly towards the tail, showing no irregular bulges or asymmetry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is darker grey/blue, and the belly area appears lighter/white, matching countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve individual dermal denticles; skin appears smooth due to distance/water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, triangular/falcate dorsal fin is visible on the back, correctly positioned.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fin on the visible side is broad and triangular, extending naturally from the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin shows the characteristic heterocercal shape with a larger upper lobe.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture is unusually smooth and uniform, lacking the subtle noise or dermal detail expected in a high-fidelity macro shot, though this may be due to water diffusion.
Background elements exhibit a 'smudged' or painterly blur rather than optical depth-of-field blur, suggesting potential generative smoothing.
